mutation_targets.rationale: Without F_LeastPrivilege, nothing forces successful operations to lie inside the permission matrix. Injecting a successful Customer GetAudit op contradicts (CustomerRole -> GetAudit not in Allowed), so the LeastPrivilege assertion must surface a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.succeeded = True and op.caller in Customer and op.kind = GetAudit }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the partial-unique-index analogue lets the model invent two PendingReview applications for the same customer, which is exactly FR-005's prohibition.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoPendingPerCustomer { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = a2.customer and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the (app, eventType) uniqueness on the audit log; injecting two distinct events for the same application and type produces a structural violation the AppendOnly assertion must catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateAuditEvent { some disj e1, e2: ApplicationEvent | e1.app = e2.app and e1.eventType = e2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without F_AuditCompleteness no fact mandates a decision event per decided application. Injecting an Approved application with zero matching approved events flunks the AuditCompleteness assertion.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingAuditEntry { some a: LoanApplication | a.status = ApprovedStatus and (no e: ApplicationEvent | e.app = a and e.eventType = EventApproved) }

mutation_targets.rationale: The PK on decisions.application_id is what guarantees SC-005. Drop the fact and inject two Decision atoms pointing at the same LoanApplication; ConcurrencySafety must report a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_TwoDecisions { some disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.application = d2.application }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without ownership-gated access, the model can let a customer successfully GET another customer's application. The injection forces such a witness and the ownership-based-access predicates fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossCustomerRead { some op: Operation | op.caller in Customer and op.kind = GetApplicationById and op.succeeded = True and some op.target and op.target.customer != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: F_AuditAttribution is the only constraint that binds an approved/rejected event's actor to staff. Removing it and injecting an Approved event whose actor is a Customer produces a clear AttributionCorrectness counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_WrongAttribution { some e: ApplicationEvent | e.eventType = EventApproved and e.actor in Customer }
